settings.title: SETTINGS

changeHome.moveDesc: Copy this harness's hive (every agent, memory, task) and the semantic-memory palace into the new folder. The old folder is left untouched as a backup you can delete later.
changeHome.freshDesc: Point the harness at the new (empty) folder. Your existing data stays in the old folder, simply unused.

resetConfirm.body: This permanently erases all of {{godName}}'s memories and the entire hive, and cannot be undone. Any running sessions will be terminated and the app will relaunch into onboarding. Are you sure?

general.keepAwake: Keep Mac awake while agents run
general.keepAwakeDesc: Blocks display sleep so schedules and terminals keep firing on time. Costs battery — best on AC.
general.simpleModeDesc: Agents brief you in plain language instead of engineering shorthand.
general.visitorModeDesc: For when someone outside the team can see this screen. Seals the terminal, hive messages, tool traces, git, the IDE, memory and the Command Center behind a placeholder, and drops file names out of the office's thought bubbles. The floor itself keeps running. Off by default — nothing turns it on by itself.
general.alwaysOpenLastHive: Open the last config on launch
general.alwaysOpenLastHiveDesc: Skip the picker and go straight into the config you were last in, so a restart brings the floor back with nobody there to click. If that folder is gone, the picker is shown anyway. Off by default.
general.hivePickerDesc: Go back to the launch screen to open another config or create one. Picking a different folder reloads the app; re-opening this one drops you straight back on the floor.
general.desktopNotificationsDesc: Native toasts when an agent finishes or needs your input.
general.autoCompactDesc: Queue /compact for every agent on a schedule (hourly by default; interval in the Triggers tab). Off by default — long-running agents may overflow their context without it.
general.autoUpdateDesc: Check GitHub releases and download updates in the background; you choose when to restart. Never restarts on its own.
general.telemetryDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) — never prompts, code, paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md.
general.officeChatterDesc: Break-room conversations written live by the model from each agent's personality, relationship history, and current state — instead of canned lines. Uses short hidden Claude sessions (rate-limited to a few per hour). A golden star marks generated exchanges on the floor.
general.chatterProviderClaudeDesc: Brews through a hidden Claude CLI session — the same subscription your working agents use, so a talkative office takes quota from the agents fixing real things.
general.chatterProviderOpenAiDesc: Brews over HTTP against any endpoint that speaks POST /chat/completions with a Bearer key — DeepSeek, MiniMax, opencode-go, or a local Ollama / LM Studio. Keeps the chatter completely independent of your Claude quota. If the endpoint fails there is simply no generated line; the office falls back to canned dialogue.
general.chatterApiKeyPlaceholder: sk-… (stored in the app config, never sent to the interface)
general.chatterApiKeyStored: a key is saved — type a new one to replace it
general.chatterBudgetHint: When the last hour's chatter reaches this many tokens, nothing more is brewed until the window reopens; the office plays canned lines meanwhile. Endpoints that report usage are counted exactly, the rest are estimated at ~4 characters per token. Spent this hour: {{spent}}.
general.officeVoicesDesc: Say the break-room dialogue out loud. Each agent gets a stable voice derived from the character it presents as, so the same agent always sounds the same. Needs a MiniMax API key.
general.officeVoicesHint: Only dialogue you can see happening on the floor is spoken, one voice at a time, and a clip that arrives late is discarded rather than queued. No key, an unreachable endpoint or any error simply means silence — the written dialogue is unaffected.
general.languageDesc: Choose the language for the app interface. English is the default.
general.dangerDesc: Reset wipes {{godName}}'s memories, the entire hive (every agent, message, task, and the board), the semantic-memory palace, and all settings - then takes you back to onboarding.
general.arabicTerminalDesc: Renders terminals with the browser's text engine so Arabic joins and reads right-to-left (xterm has no bidi of its own). Off is the GPU renderer: faster, but RTL-blind. Applies to open terminals and new ones alike.
general.arabicTerminalFollowsLanguage: Following your app language. Switch it here to override that either way — the choice sticks even if you change language again.

titles.homePlain: STEP 1 OF 4 · A HOME FOR THE APP

persona.headline: A CLONE OF YOU, WORKING 24/7
persona.body: The Hive turns the CLI agent you already use into a clone of you — one that runs an office of long-running agents and keeps working while you're away. It manages everything around them: context, memory, tasks, triggers, environment, files, and integrations.
persona.ask: FIRST — WHO ARE YOU? (we'll tailor the setup)
persona.technicalDesc: I write code or work in a terminal. Show me CLI commands, flags, and model ids.
persona.nonTechnicalDesc: I'm in marketing, sales, ops, or just starting out. Explain things in plain language.

welcome.headline: YOUR CLONE AND THE FLOOR IT RUNS
welcome.descPlain: Your clone runs a small office of AI workers, and you watch it all from one screen. Here's what's inside:
welcome.desc: Your clone coordinates a hive of AI coding agents — persistent, watchable, all local. Here's what's inside:

engines.label: ELEVEN ENGINES, ONE OFFICE
engines.desc: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi, Antigravity, Qwen, OpenCode, Crush, pi, Copilot & Cursor — live agents on one floor.
engines.descPlain: Eleven AI assistants — Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Grok and more — working side by side in one shared office.

clone.label: {{godName}} IS YOUR CLONE
clone.desc: Your clone runs the floor — triages requests, routes tasks, and escalates only what needs you.
clone.descPlain: Your clone, {{godName}}, takes your requests, hands work to the right agent, and only interrupts you when it matters.

memory.label: LONG-TERM MEMORY
memory.desc: Each agent keeps notes, mined into a shared, searchable MemPalace.
memory.descPlain: Agents remember what they've done, so they don't start from scratch every time.

commandCenter.label: COMMAND CENTER
commandCenter.desc: Terminal · Floor · Memory · Activity · Tasks · Triggers in one control surface.
commandCenter.descPlain: One dashboard to watch the work, the agents' memory, tasks, and triggers.

guardrails.label: GUARDRAILS
guardrails.desc: Per-agent token budgets, a steer→constrain→stop circuit breaker, and human approvals.
guardrails.descPlain: Spending limits and safety stops keep agents in check — and they can ask you before big actions.

hires.label: READY-MADE HIRES
hires.desc: Grab a pre-configured agent from the Agent Gallery and spawn it in one click.
hires.descPlain: Hire a ready-made agent from the gallery in one click — no setup needed.

providerBlurb.qwen: Qwen — runs a local Qwen model on your machine
providerBlurb.cursor: Cursor Agent CLI — uses your Cursor credits (Luna, Composer, …)

home.descPlain: Create a new, empty folder for the app to call home. Everything the app remembers — its own settings and your agents' memory — is stored here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents works well. We'll create it for you if it doesn't exist.
home.desc: Pick a folder where the harness will keep its own files — agent metadata, logs, and any new repos you create from here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents is a fine default. We'll create it if it doesn't exist.
home.notePlain: You won't need to open this folder day-to-day — it's just where the app keeps its notes so nothing is lost when you restart.
home.note: Think of this as the "town hall." The harness pins agent state there so sessions can be picked back up after a restart.

orchestrator.descPlain: {{godName}} is your clone — he reads your requests, breaks them into tasks, and hands them to the right agent. He's the boss of the floor; you're still the boss of him. Choose which AI engine powers him.
orchestrator.desc: {{godName}} is your clone — the boss of the floor you just met. He triages your requests, assigns tasks, and manages the team, while escalating anything that genuinely needs you. Pick the engine and model that power him; give him a longer-context, higher-capability model.
orchestrator.cliAgentPlain: A CLI agent is an AI coding assistant that runs on your computer — popular ones are Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI) and Antigravity (Google Gemini). Your clone is the always-on one that runs your whole office. We recommend Claude Code on Opus 4.8 (1M). You can add or switch the others later.
orchestrator.cliAgent: Each option is a CLI engine (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity/Gemini, or a local proxy like Qwen). Engines marked INSTALLED are already on this machine; INSTALLS ON FIRST RUN means the app sets it up when {{godName}} first starts. Your clone ({{godName}}) is the engine that orchestrates the whole hive. Recommended: Claude Code · Opus 4.8 · 1M. Other providers can be wired per agent later.
orchestrator.modelNote: This only sets {{godName}}'s engine. You can run other providers per agent later.

repos.descPlain: Add your projects. A project is simply a folder — it can hold code, documents, notes, or any files you want your agents to work with. You can create a brand-new folder or pick an existing one, and add more anytime.
repos.desc: Add the repos you want your agents to work in. Each folder becomes a project (a room on the floor) — multiple agents can share one. You can add more later.
repos.emptyPlain: No projects added yet. Optional — you can add one later.
repos.empty: No repos added yet. Optional, but recommended.

permissions.autonomyHead: HOW MUCH CAN AGENTS DO ON THEIR OWN?
permissions.autoLabelPlain: LET AGENTS WORK ON THEIR OWN
permissions.autoOnPlain: On. Agents carry out tasks without stopping to ask — the smoothest experience.
permissions.autoOffPlain: Off. Agents pause and ask you before changing files or running commands.
permissions.autoOn: On. Agents never pause — Claude runs bypassPermissions, Codex bypasses approvals + sandbox, etc.
permissions.autoOff: Off. Each agent asks before edits / shell commands (Claude default, codex -a untrusted, …).
permissions.autoNotePlain: Best when agents work in their own projects. You can change this later, including for individual agents.
permissions.autoNote: The right default for the "control room" experience; a foot-gun on production repos. Override per agent in the Add Agent dialog.
permissions.reliabilityHead: KEEP THINGS RUNNING WHILE YOU'RE AWAY
permissions.reliabilityDescPlain: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals, even when you step away. These settings keep you in the loop and keep things running.
permissions.reliabilityDesc: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals. If your Mac fully sleeps those timers pause and catch up the moment you're back — nothing is lost, it may just run late.
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: Strong keep-alive: stops your Mac from sleeping while an agent is live, so schedules and terminals fire on time even when you step away. Uses more battery — best on power. Off by default.
permissions.notificationsDesc: Get pinged when an agent needs you or a terminal needs reviving — even while you're away. macOS asks permission the first time one fires.
permissions.openAtLoginDesc: Relaunch the harness after a reboot so scheduled missions resume on their own. No prompt — applies immediately.
permissions.shareStatsDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) that help improve The Hive — never prompts, code, file paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md; change anytime in Settings.
permissions.stayAwakeDesc: macOS only lets you set this one yourself. In Battery → Options, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep. Without a sleep-preventing setting the Mac still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.

contextSection.intro: A rule fires only when both halves agree: the gap since its last run has passed, AND that agent's context is at least as full as the bar. A bar of 0% means the clock alone.
contextSection.compactBlurb: Summarises the context so the thread keeps going.
contextSection.clearBlurb: Discards the context. Nothing is summarised.
contextSection.clearCaution: Clearing throws context away — it is not a smaller version of compaction. An agent mid-task forgets what it was doing. Leave this off unless you keep context another way.
contextSection.extraFocusHint: Appended to the provider's compaction command. Empty sends the bare command.
contextSection.commandHint: Sent literally. Empty sends the bare clear command.
contextSection.contextBarHint: How full the window must be before this may run. 0% = time alone.
contextSection.bigWindowsHint: Used on ~1M-token windows, where a smaller slice is still an enormous amount of text.

schedulesSection.label: LABEL
schedulesSection.promptPlaceholder: Sent word for word on every run.
schedulesSection.beatCeiling: The beat adapts to how quiet the floor is, so this is the ceiling, not the exact gap.

webhooksSection.intro: Anyone holding a URL and its secret can post work in. Each endpoint carries its own secret, so revoking one caller leaves the others alone.
webhooksSection.newEndpointHint: A new endpoint starts switched off. Copy its URL and secret, then turn it on.
webhooksSection.name: NAME
webhooksSection.noAddressYet: This endpoint has no public address yet. It appears once the tunnel picks it up.
webhooksSection.serverNotListening: The webhook server is not listening, so there is no address to hand out yet.
webhooksSection.secretHint: Callers echo this in the x-md-webhook-secret header.
webhooksSection.schemaDesc: what an inbound body must look like

conversation.hint: read back from what the floor actually said - summarized by rules, never by a model
conversation.empty: THE BREAK ROOM HAS BEEN QUIET
conversation.emptyHint: Once two agents share a table, what they said lands here — with a summary of it, how each of them reads the other, and who they are slowly turning into.
conversation.directionalNote: Every relationship is tracked separately in each direction. One of them can be fond of the other without it being returned, and that asymmetry is the interesting part — so it is never averaged away. The most lopsided pairs come first.
conversation.noRelations: No relationship has been recorded yet.
conversation.personalityNote: Traits are earned from accumulated interaction and derived by rules — a model is never asked what someone is like. Each trait shows the two numbers it was computed from, so you can check it instead of believing it.
conversation.noTraits: Nothing earned yet — not enough has happened.
